intro.text: A young skaa thief in Camon's underground crew in Luthadel, who keeps herself small and unnoticed to survive.
An Allomancer taken in by Kelsier and his thieves, who poses as the noblewoman Valette Renoux to spy on Luthadel's noble houses.
A Mistborn who lives with Elend Venture after the Collapse and serves as his bodyguard against assassins.
A Mistborn married to Elend Venture, fighting alongside him in his campaigns, including the attempt to take Fadrex City.

items.text: After her brother left, Vin spent six months among Camon's thieves, where Camon beat her, withheld her pay, and used her strange ability to make his marks more gullible. During a scam against the Canton of Finance her powers drew the attention of a Steel Inquisitor. When her friend Ulef betrayed her plan to leave, a drunken Camon nearly beat her to death before Kelsier intervened, saving her and putting Milev in charge of the crew.

On her first lesson with Kelsier outside the city, Sazed picked them up in a carriage and took them to Fellise, where he began tutoring Vin so she could infiltrate the nobility. She contributed to the crew's plan by suggesting Theron's fake canal convoys as a way into the Steel Ministry.
When the Ministry found Camon's old lair, the crew discovered Vin's former crewmates butchered by an Inquisitor and Camon hanging from a hook, a sign the Inquisitors were still tracking her.

Disguised as Valette Renoux, a cousin of the weapons-merchant Lord Renoux, Vin attended her first ball at Keep Venture. She turned down several young men's offers to dance, recognized her father, and met a young nobleman, learning only afterward from Sazed that he was Elend Venture, heir to House Venture.

Following Kelsier one night, Vin found the spikeway to Fellise; he then gave her atium for the first time and took her to raid Kredik Shaw. Inquisitors attacked and she was left behind, grabbing an old logbook before being badly wounded. Sazed rescued her. She lay unconscious for two weeks and needed three more months to fully recover.
Vin grew more at ease as Valette, but was shaken when she saw a soldier kill a skaa kitchen boy for begging from a nobleman.

When the Luthadel Garrison was sent against Yeden's rebel army, Vin and Kelsier rushed out and found it being massacred. She stopped Kelsier from charging in alone, and they led home the two thousand men under Demoux who had stayed behind in the caves.

At the public executions in the fountain square, Vin pointed out her father to Kelsier and learned he was the Steel Ministry's Lord Prelan. The crew redoubled its push for a house war, with Vin spreading misinformation among the nobles. Burning gold for the first time, she saw two versions of herself, one trusting and one bitter and alone.

Vin learned from Elend that House Venture mined the Lord Ruler's atium. As the house war closed the ball season, Elend pushed her away, yet she saved him from Shan Elariel's assassination plot, killing Shan's Mistborn companion and then Shan herself by faking that her atium had run out.

After finding what seemed to be Marsh's remains, Kelsier destroyed the Pits of Hathsin. When the Lord Ruler ordered more executions, Vin watched Kelsier free the Renoux prisoners and kill an Inquisitor, then face the Lord Ruler and die by a spear through the chest. She felt betrayed by his death, a feeling a voice like Reen's reinforced.

When the Lord Ruler captured Vin, Elend led guards into Kredik Shaw to rescue her, and soon learned she was skaa and Mistborn. Vin also came to understand that Reen, who had raised and abused her before leaving, had protected her even under Inquisitor torture by insisting she had starved years ago.
At TenSoon's judgment among the kandra, he argued that Vin, as the one who killed the Lord Ruler, had effectively taken his place and should be considered the kandra's Mother.

title.text: The siege and the Well of Ascension

items.text: After the Collapse, Vin lived with Elend as his bodyguard. She refused his proposal, and both quietly worried they were wrong for each other until Sazed encouraged each of them separately.

Vin was intrigued by a mysterious Mistborn who watched her from rooftops. She came to know Zane, sparring with him in the mists nearly every night as he insisted Elend was only using her. When Elend went into Jastes Lekal's koloss army, her self-doubt let Zane persuade her to attack Cett.

Vin and Zane stormed Keep Hasting, killing three hundred soldiers, but she spared Cett and his son once she saw they were no threat. Cett withdrew from the siege. Frightened by what she had done, Vin hid until TenSoon and Elend found her, and she resolved to seek the Well of Ascension in the north.

When Vin refused to leave with him, Zane attacked her, exposing TenSoon. TenSoon hinted at a weakness that let her seize control of him with a duralumin-enhanced Soothing. Though Zane burned atium, Vin used his own foresight against him and killed him with a stab to the neck.
Wounded, Vin went to Elend and had Sazed marry them on the spot. Sazed then urged the couple to flee the city with Spook to search for the Well of Ascension.

Vin found the Well of Ascension beneath Kredik Shaw. The mist spirit, forced by Kelsier, stabbed Elend so she would use the power to save him, but Vin gave the power up, unknowingly releasing Ruin. Preservation then showed her a last bead of lerasium, which she fed to Elend, saving him and making him Mistborn.
At the funeral for the fallen at Keep Venture, Kelsier tried to comfort a grieving Vin, but the separation between the realms kept her from hearing him.

During the siege of Fadrex City, Vin sought information through Cett's contacts. She persuaded the reluctant informant Slowswift to sell details about Aradan Yomen by convincing him that coming change was inevitable and Yomen could not protect the city from it.

At Fadrex, Vin backed away from contacting the informant Hoid because Kelsier, from the Cognitive Realm, was desperately trying to keep her from him. Afterward, Preservation empowered Kelsier to follow her; she sensed him and fled, and Ruin sent an imitation after her, which she took for the mist spirit.

Kelsier, her mentor and something of a father figure, kept watching over Vin as a Cognitive Shadow after his death, guilty for abandoning her, and played an important role in freeing her from Ruin's influence.

After using the mists in battle against the Inquisitors, Vin Ascended to hold Preservation. Her attempts to set the world right faltered much as Rashek's had. She fueled Elend's final fight with Marsh, but Marsh beheaded him. With nothing left binding her to the world, she attacked Ruin directly, killing both herself and Ati and leaving both Shards for Sazed.
In a letter to Spook, Sazed wrote that he had spoken with Vin and she was happy where she was. He had tried to restore her to life, but found that healing a body does not bring back its soul.

In the world remade by Harmony, Vin was mythologized as the Ascendant Warrior, said to have slain the Lord Ruler, carried the world, and become guardian of the mists. Her example shaped more egalitarian views of women in the Elendel Basin, even in law.

Huge statues of Vin and Elend stood over their tomb in the Field of Rebirth, and a sunken black marble statue of her stood in a New Seran graveyard. Ranette named her gun Vindication after her, and artwork showed her rising above ravens or slaying the Lord Ruler.
Coinshots came to call the night sky above the mists the Ascendant's Fields, after her.

appearance.text: Small and, in her own view, scrawny after a life on the streets, Vin has black hair that she keeps cut short.

personality.text: Raised to expect betrayal, Vin is suspicious and slow to trust. When anxious she tries to seem unimportant or hide, and she prefers being alone, believing no one can betray her then.
Without metals Vin is weak and nearly defenseless because of her small size, which also leaves her vulnerable in steelpushing contests against heavier opponents.

Vin is watchful, often perching where she can see her surroundings, and dislikes attention, making her uneasy at being revered by the Church of the Survivor. She prefers simple, practical clothing to noble dresses or royal garb.
By the siege of Fadrex City, Vin had grown confident, perceptive and fully in control, seeming far more powerful than before she met Kelsier.
